title: Claude marketplace transition leaves plugin version metadata behind
symptom: During the isolated macOS Claude 0.2.3 to 0.2.4 lifecycle transition, the installer exited zero and Claude moved the boxbox-plugins marketplace to the 0.2.4 permanent root. The immediately following plugin listing still reported version 0.2.3 and the cached 0.2.3 installPath. Claude's own installer output said the already-installed plugin would load in place from the new 0.2.4 marketplace root and that `claude plugin update boxbox@boxbox-plugins` would re-record its version from 0.2.3 to 0.2.4. The lifecycle verifier therefore stopped rather than treating the mixed listing as an accepted update.

rootCause.summary: The installer repointed Claude's local marketplace but did not explicitly run the host's plugin-update transition or verify the resulting installed-plugin identity. Claude keeps marketplace source and installed-plugin version/cache metadata as separate state, so exit zero from marketplace installation alone can leave the marketplace on 0.2.4 while the installed record remains 0.2.3. The evidence does not establish that old plugin code executed.

requestedOutcome: Define and verify a deterministic Claude transition procedure whose post-transition marketplace, installed-plugin version, install path and effective plugin root all identify the intended artifact, while preserving the prior working installation and user-owned data on refusal or failure.
decisions: Treat an exit-zero installer result as insufficient when Claude's machine-readable marketplace and plugin listings disagree about the active version/root.

When the exact owned Claude plugin record remains stale after marketplace registration, use one exact user-scoped plugin update and then require marketplace, installed-plugin, manifest, runtime and engine identity to agree before reporting success.
Fail closed after possible host mutation and retain recoverable filesystem state; do not infer host rollback from installer failure.
Keep the historical 0.2.3 input classified as an uncommitted lifecycle fixture, not a released or approved baseline.

actions.description: Inspect the retained macOS and WSL transition failures and establish how Claude separates marketplace source from installed-plugin version/cache metadata.
Measure one explicit `claude plugin update boxbox@boxbox-plugins --scope user` in the retained isolated macOS profile, including identity, effective runtime and preservation.
Complete independent source and GLM review of the bounded installer repair, including capability, exact identity, shared/same-version ownership and signaled-child retention gates.
Run and independently review the complete bounded local-candidate Claude/Codex lifecycle and supported HUD ownership matrix across macOS, Linux/WSL and native Windows.
Record the terminal hosted macOS engine-smoke result for candidate workflow 39646320662; keep workflow-level completion separate from the already reviewed native lifecycle matrix.

history.summary: The first terminal isolated macOS Claude lifecycle stopped after a direct 0.2.3 to 0.2.4 attempt returned success and moved the marketplace root to 0.2.4 while the plugin listing retained version and cache path 0.2.3. Claude explicitly recommended `plugin update` to re-record the version.

A separate WSL Claude 2.1.280 lifecycle reproduced the stale installed-version record. Durable diagnosis confirmed that installation repointed the marketplace without an explicit plugin update or sufficient post-transition identity acceptance; neither failed cell proves old-code execution.

One authorized isolated macOS `plugin update` probe re-recorded version/cache 0.2.4 and verified the intended marketplace/runtime identity with preservation intact. The probe was kept separate from the original failed lifecycle and does not establish installer or lifecycle completion.

A bounded shared phase/identity repair entered source review. Mandatory review gates, including the remaining same-version/shared-registration guard, remain open; no new candidate lifecycle has passed and the issue remains investigating.

The final frozen installer repair closed pre-mutation scoped-update capability, exact marketplace path/installLocation, single-entry catalog ownership, parent-side same-version/shared-catalog protection and signaled-child retention. Independent source closure and GLM static audit passed with no mandatory findings; native acceptance remained separate.

A distinct exact local unpublished candidate completed the macOS Claude core and HUD cells. The core accepted 0.2.4 only after exact plugin/marketplace/cache/runtime/engine agreement, preserved the historical rollback boundary and user bytes, and removed final registration; HUD proof remained limited to isolated configuration ownership. Linux, Windows and final clean/CI evidence remain pending, so the issue moved to verifying rather than resolved.

The exact local dirty-source candidate 1f1343e9… completed all six macOS/WSL/native-Windows core lifecycle cells and four supported macOS/WSL HUD ownership cells. Independent review passed the bounded matrix while preserving non-CI, authentication/UI/hook, Windows-HUD and publication limits.

The clean staging source 66eb978… produced CI archive ebfe6a77…. Independent review passed its exact macOS Codex/Claude core and HUD ownership cells. Remote final-CI lifecycle review and hosted macOS smoke were still pending, so the workflow and issue remained verifying.

The first independent review of the clean-CI remote native cells was INCOMPLETE because the compact evidence copy omitted the 848 raw stdout/stderr files referenced by six lifecycle reports. This was an evidence-review gap, not a demonstrated product lifecycle failure; the original review remains unchanged.

A combined 854-file digest manifest and all 848 referenced command logs closed the raw-evidence gap. Independent review passed the exact ebfe6a77… WSL/native-Windows core and supported WSL HUD cells; combined with the separately reviewed macOS cells, the clean-CI archive has six core and four HUD ownership passes. PR run 39646325026 also passed hosted Ubuntu/macOS source verification. Hosted macOS candidate smoke remained queued, so neither workflow-level PASS nor issue resolution was claimed.
